pack.title: Surveys and Differences in a Coastal Town

provenance.author: Dual Dictionary project — AI-assisted original source
provenance.rightsStatement: Original reading drafted with coding assistant for this pilot; no personal learner data.

lessons.title: Surveys and Differences in a Coastal Town
lessons.objective: Learners will understand and use 'carry out a survey' and 'draw a distinction between' in academic and everyday contexts.

reading.text: Researchers will carry out a survey about transport choices in a coastal town. They must draw a distinction between occasional visitors and people who travel to work every day. The council will use these findings to decide whether a new bus route is needed.

sentences.text: Researchers will carry out a survey about transport choices in a coastal town.
They must draw a distinction between occasional visitors and people who travel to work every day.
The council will use these findings to decide whether a new bus route is needed.

targets.meaningEn: to conduct a survey by asking people questions to collect information
targets.meaningVi: tiến hành một cuộc khảo sát

targets.meaningEn: to recognize and show the difference between two or more things
targets.meaningVi: chỉ ra sự khác biệt giữa

exercises.prompt: In s1: 'Researchers will carry out a survey about transport choices in a coastal town.' What does 'carry out a survey' mean here?

options.text: to look at the final results after a survey is finished
options.explanation: This is wrong because looking at results happens after collecting information, while the sentence describes collecting information by asking questions.

options.text: to conduct a survey by asking people questions to collect information
options.explanation: This is correct because it matches asking people questions to collect information about transport (tiến hành một cuộc khảo sát).

options.text: to cancel a survey because people do not want to answer
options.explanation: Wrong: Cancelling means stopping or deciding not to conduct a survey; carrying out a survey means conducting it.

exercises.explanation: The researchers will ask people questions to collect information, so b is the only correct meaning.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 'carry out a survey' naturally?

options.text: Our class carried out a survey about lunch choices last week.
options.explanation: This is correct because the collocation 'carried out a survey about' and grammar are natural and correct.

options.text: Our class carried out a survey in lunch choices last week.
options.explanation: This is wrong because the preposition 'in' is incorrect and must be changed to 'about' or 'on'.

options.text: Our class carried out survey about lunch choices last week.
options.explanation: This is wrong because the article 'a' is missing and must be added before 'survey'.

exercises.explanation: Only a uses correct grammar and collocation, so a is the only correct choice.

exercises.prompt: In s2: 'They must draw a distinction between occasional visitors and people who travel to work every day.' What does 'draw a distinction between' mean here?

options.text: to ignore the differences and treat two groups as the same
options.explanation: This is wrong because ignoring differences is the opposite of recognizing and showing the difference.

options.text: to invite both groups to travel together on the same bus
options.explanation: This is wrong because inviting groups to travel together does not mean recognizing and showing a difference.

options.text: to recognize and show the difference between two or more things
options.explanation: Correct: They must show the difference between visitors and daily commuters (chỉ ra sự khác biệt giữa).

exercises.explanation: They need to recognize and show the difference between two groups, so c is the only correct meaning.

exercises.prompt: Which sentence uses 'draw a distinction between' naturally?

options.text: The report draws a distinction between short-term visitors to daily commuters.
options.explanation: This is wrong because 'to' is incorrect and must be changed to 'and' in the pattern 'between A and B'.

options.text: The report draws a distinction between short-term visitors and daily commuters.
options.explanation: This is correct because it uses the natural pattern 'draws a distinction between A and B' with two comparable noun phrases.

options.text: The report draws distinction between short-term visitors and daily commuters.
options.explanation: This is wrong because the article 'a' is missing and must be added before 'distinction'.

exercises.explanation: Only b follows the natural pattern with correct grammar, so b is the only correct choice.

exercises.prompt: You are a student helping a new classmate understand the school library. Write 2-3 sentences explaining the difference between regular books you can borrow and reference books you can only read in the library. Use the phrase 'draw a distinction between'.
exercises.sampleAnswer: Welcome to our school library! I want to draw a distinction between regular books, which you can borrow for two weeks, and reference books, which you can only read in the library.
selfCheck: I used the exact phrase 'draw a distinction between'.
I named two different things and explained the difference.
I wrote 2-3 sentences in a friendly, helpful tone for a classmate.
exercises.explanation: Compare with the model and self-assess; no automatic grade.
